references.text: Abraham's servant asked that the right woman would say 'Drink, my lord' - exactly what Rebekah says here, fulfilling the sign.
The servant recounts the event to Rebekah's family, including that she said 'Drink' and hurriedly lowered her jar - a direct parallel to this verse.
A similar well scene where Jacob meets Rachel and waters her sheep, a pattern of meetings at wells leading to marriage.
The call to hospitality toward strangers, for some have entertained angels without knowing it - Rebekah's willingness to serve a stranger at the well illustrates this attitude.
The virtuous woman reaches out her hands to the needy - Rebekah's quick and willing service reflects this character.
The same event told from two perspectives (Rebekah's actions and Eliezer's account) confirming God's guidance.
The same event from Eliezer's perspective confirming Rebekah's role as God's chosen one.
The same event from Eliezer's perspective emphasizing God's providence and Rebekah's immediate response.
